\section*{Question 4}

A particle moves along the \(x\)-axis with velocity at time \(t \geq 0\) given by \(v(t)=-1+e^{1-t}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the acceleration of the particle at time \(t=3\).
\item[(b)] Is the speed of the particle increasing at time \(t=3\) ? Give a reason for your answer.
\item[(c)] Find all values of \(t\) at which the particle changes direction. Justify your answer.
\item[(d)] Find the total distance traveled by the particle over the time interval \(0 \leq t \leq 3\).
\item[(a)] \(a(t)=v^{\prime}(t)=-e^{1-t}\)
\[
a(3)=-e^{-2}
\]
\item[(b)] \(a(3)<0\)
\[
v(3)=-1+e^{-2}<0
\]
Speed is increasing since \(v(3)<0\) and \(a(3)<0\).
\item[(c)] \(v(t)=0\) when \(1=e^{1-t}\), so \(t=1\).
\[
v(t)>0 \text { for } t<1 \text { and } v(t)<0 \text { for } t>1 \text {. }
\]
Therefore, the particle changes direction at \(t=1\).
\item[(d)] Distance \(=\int_{0}^{3}|v(t)| d t\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& =\int_{0}^{1}\left(-1+e^{1-t}\right) d t+\int_{1}^{3}\left(1-e^{1-t}\right) d t \\
& =\left(-t-\left.e^{1-t}\right|_{0} ^{1}\right)+\left(t+\left.e^{1-t}\right|_{1} ^{3}\right) \\
& =(-1-1+e)+\left(3+e^{-2}-1-1\right) \\
& =e+e^{-2}-1
\end{aligned}
\]
OR
\[
\begin{aligned}
& x(t)=-t-e^{1-t} \\
& x(0)=-e \\
& x(1)=-2 \\
& \begin{aligned}
& x(3)=-e^{-2}-3 \\
& \text { Distance }=(x(1)-x(0))+(x(1)-x(3)) \\
&=(-2+e)+\left(1+e^{-2}\right) \\
&=e+e^{-2}-1
\end{aligned}
\end{aligned}
\]
\end{itemize}
\[
2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}
1: v^{\prime}(t) \\
1: a(3)
\end{array}\right.
\]

1 : answer with reason
\(2:\left\{\begin{array}{c}1: \text { solves } v(t)=0 \text { to } \\ \text { get } t=1 \\ 1: \text { justifies change in } \\ \text { direction at } t=1\end{array}\right.\)
\(4:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { limits } \\ 1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { antidifferentiation } \\ 1: \text { evaluation }\end{array}\right.\)

OR
\(4:\left\{\begin{array}{c}1: \text { any antiderivative } \\ 1: \text { evaluates } x(t) \text { when } \\ t=0,1,3 \\ 1: \text { evaluates distance } \\ \text { between points } \\ 1: \text { evaluates total distance }\end{array}\right.\)
